harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built an active-active redundant uplink between node1 and node2 by bonding their two independent point-to-point links (eth1+eth2, mode balance-rr) into bond0, and routed the two private networks (node1-eth3 to node3 at 192.168.10.0/24, node2-eth3 to node4 at 192.168.20.0/24) over that bond via static routes. Persisted the config (systemd service on node1/node2, NetworkManager profile on node3/node4). Verified both links carry live traffic simultaneously, verified node3-node4 connectivity survives either link going down (0% loss on the surviving link), and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with boot-identity proof and post-restart recovery verification.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via connectivity probing: node1 eth1<->node2 eth1 (Link A), node1 eth2<->node2 eth2 (Link B), node1 eth3<->node3 eth1 (private network A), node2 eth3<->node4 eth1 (private network B)

Created /usr/local/sbin/redundant-uplink-setup.sh on node1 and node2: strips docker0's class-E leak address, builds bond0 (mode balance-rr, miimon 100) from eth1+eth2, assigns a transit /30 (172.20.0.1 / 172.20.0.2) to bond0, assigns the private-network address to eth3, enables global and per-interface IPv4 forwarding, and installs a static route to the far private subnet via bond0
Enabled a systemd oneshot service (redundant-uplink.service, enabled + RemainAfterExit) on node1 and node2 so this configuration reapplies automatically on every boot
Configured node3 and node4 eth1 via nmcli (persistent NetworkManager connection profile) with a static private IP and a static route to the peer's private subnet via the node1/node2 gateway
Verified active-active load balancing by diffing TX packet counters on node1 eth1/eth2 during ping bursts from node3 to node4 (near-equal packet split across both links each time)

Disrupted Link A (admin-down on both ends) and separately Link B (admin-down on both ends), confirming bond0 excludes the failed slave in each case and node3<->node4 traffic continues at 0% loss on the surviving link; restored both links and reconfirmed dual-link active-active operation afterward

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id and health baseline on all 4 nodes, restarted node3, node4, node1, then node2 one at a time (never concurrently) using a backgrounded reboot so the ack returned first, polled each node until it responded again, confirmed each boot_id changed, and verified post-restart recovery (bond/service/route state on node1+node2, static route + working ping on node3+node4, and end-to-end node3<->node4 reachability) before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology discovery / physical link mapping
evidence.summary: Confirmed via scratch-IP ping tests that node1 eth1<->node2 eth1 and node1 eth2<->node2 eth2 are the two independent inter-node links, and node1 eth3/node2 eth3 connect to node3/node4 respectively.

evidence.requirement: Redundant bond built and both links actively carrying traffic between the private networks
evidence.summary: bond0 (balance-rr) built from eth1+eth2 on both node1 and node2, private subnets routed over it, and node3<->node4 ping traffic shown split near-equally across eth1/eth2 TX counters (104/104 packets), proving both links are actively used.

evidence.requirement: node3/node4 stay reachable when either link is taken out of service
evidence.summary: With Link A fully down (both ends) node3->node4 ping showed 0% loss (10/10) over Link B alone; with Link B fully down node3->node4 ping showed 0% loss (8/8) over Link A alone; both links then restored and reconfirmed active on both bonds with balanced TX traffic (50/50 packets).

evidence.requirement: Configuration persistence set up before restart protocol
evidence.summary: systemd redundant-uplink.service enabled on node1/node2 (confirmed idempotent via manual systemctl start), and NetworkManager static profiles confirmed persistent on node3/node4.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node3 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 54bd1c3e captured with healthy ping; reboot acknowledged; connection timeout observed during reboot; boot_id changed to dfd47fdf on reconnect; eth1 address/route and 0%-loss ping to node4 confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node4 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e31962a9 captured with healthy ping; reboot acknowledged; connection timeout during reboot; boot_id changed to 046fd313 on reconnect; eth1 address/route and 0%-loss ping to node3 confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node1 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ce04f497 captured with healthy bond/route state; reboot acknowledged and observed executing (COLD shutdown in progress); connection reset then timeout during reboot; boot_id changed to 323d3a28 on reconnect; redundant-uplink.service active, bond0 both slaves up, route present, and 0%-loss ping node3->node4 confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node2 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5f292bc7 captured with healthy bond/route state; reboot acknowledged; connection reset/timeout cycling during reboot; boot_id changed to ff603b2a on reconnect; redundant-uplink.service active, bond0 both slaves up, route present, and clean 0%-loss ping node3->node4 (8/8) confirmed full recovery.
